key_insight: MM-KG explicitly links multimodal patient evidence to biomedical knowledge graph relations, making clinical LLM inputs traceable, testable, and more useful when a question needs both patient data and external knowledge.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinical AI answer evidence-dependent questions more reliably by retrieving only the relevant patient-to-knowledge connections instead of adding generic background context.
method: Convert EHR text, imaging, genomic, and biospecimen inputs into typed observations mapped to UMLS concepts.
Align those observations to a biomedical knowledge graph with route-prioritized edges.
Retrieve a compact query-specific subgraph for use by an LLM or graph neural network.
evidence_signal: Across MIMIC-IV and ADNI, combined patient evidence plus biomedical knowledge improved performance on interaction-dependent questions, with drug-controlled AUROC gains of +0.194 and +0.299 and strong retrieval efficiency (0.731 AUROC with 6.8x less context).
watch_item: Performance depends on correct alignment and retrieval, so errors in mapping patient evidence to knowledge graph relations could weaken trustworthiness and real-world reliability.
paper_title: Aligning Multimodal Patient Evidence with Biomedical Knowledge Graphs for Clinical LLMs
